extraction.Name: Thomas Twiss
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 320 acre allotment at the time it was issued, for he did not want to pay taxes; but he was advised by the Indian Agency that, if he did not take it, he would finally lose the land through tax assessments, he therefore took the patent
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Isaac H. Chase, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $500.00; sold to Fay Balls, of Rapid City, South Dakota, Mr. Balls taking over the mortgage, paying off the taxes which had again accumulated from 1921; and paid deponent $150.00 in cash and delivered him on the deal four cows, valued at $50.00 each
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in taxes, and, in 1921, he mortgaged the allotment to Isaac H. Chase, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $500.00, and then he paid his taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: he works as a laborer on other peoples farms, which constitutes his only source of income
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent and in good health; wife died in 1926; has five children to support, all having good health; has a 20 acre piece of heirship land which he farms; finds it hard to get along on his income; considers he got a pretty poor price for his land; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; document notarized December 7, 1928 in Shannon County, South Dakota | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
